title: The 5 smallest countries on Earth
sources: Vatican City 0.44 km², about 1,000 people: UN data (data.un.org)
Central Park 341 ha = 3.41 km², 4.0 km × 0.8 km: Central Park facts
Monaco 2.08 km², about 38,000 people, most densely populated country: IMSEE via Hello Monaco; Australian DFAT country brief
Nauru 21 km², no official capital: Britannica
Tuvalu 26 km², nine islands, highest point 4.6 m: ASPRS 'Tuvalu' (2019)
San Marino 61 km², enclave of Italy, oldest constitutional republic, founded 301: Wikipedia via mirror

script.say: The smallest country on Earth is so tiny, New York's Central Park is almost eight times bigger.
These are the five smallest countries in the world.
Sixty-one square kilometers, about the size of Manhattan.
It's completely surrounded by Italy, and it's the oldest republic still standing, founded in the year three hundred and one.
Twenty-six square kilometers, scattered across nine tiny islands in the Pacific.
Its highest point is just four point six meters above the sea.
Twenty-one square kilometers. One single island, and no official capital city.
Just two square kilometers. That's smaller than Central Park.
Yet about thirty-eight thousand people live here. The most crowded country on the planet.
Less than half a square kilometer. Around a thousand people. And still its own country, with its own flag.
Which one would you visit? Spin the globe yourself, on Bhoogol.
